# IVX IA Chat Infrastructure — Architecture Research Report

## 1. Mobile Chat UI — `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`

**File:** `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`
**Line count:** 8,716 lines

### Features
This is a **monolithic** chat screen — one of the largest single components in the codebase. It implements:

- **Message rendering** via `FlatList` (inverted, WhatsApp-style) with `MessageBubble` and `ExecutionConsoleBubble` components
- **Message deduplication** — 3-layer dedup: optimistic→persistent, transient→persistent (body-match), and taskId-based dedup for execution-mode responses
- **Durable local mirror** — every rendered owner/assistant turn is written to a local shadow store so conversation survives reloads/route changes
- **Conversation ID adoption** — canonical conversation ID is adopted from backend responses and persisted via AsyncStorage; restored on mount
- **Composer** — text input with auto-resize, draft persistence (text + failed attachments), pinned messages
- **Voice transcription** — `expo-audio` recording → `transcribeAudioRecording()` mutation
- **File attachments** — `expo-document-picker`, upload progress tracking, image/video/file types
- **Message search** — in-memory filter over `displayedMessages`
- **Reply context** — quote-reply to specific messages
- **Slash commands** — 12+ built-in `/help`, `/status`, `/clear`, `/reconnect`, `/probe`, `/broadcast`, `/knowledge`, `/proof`, `/risk`, `/incident`, `/deps`, `/heal`, `/replay`, `/brain` + dynamic Command Brain commands
- **Prompt templates** — 3 owner templates: `deal_review`, `investor_reply`, `document_summary`
- **Owner diagnostics panel** — QA panel, watchdog drawer, staged timeout banner, backend audit, runtime debug snapshot
- **Live Work detection** — regex patterns detect when a sent message kicks off real IVX work (Supabase check, deploy, scan, fix, audit, build) and surfaces an inline "Live Work" button
- **Senior Developer Worker integration** — `ExecutionConsoleBubble` renders live-polling execution status for worker jobs
- **Control Tower** — live intelligence snapshot, control room status query
- **Auth state machine** — `OwnerAIAuthState`: AUTH_INITIALIZING → SIGNED_OUT / SESSION_REFRESHING / SIGNED_IN_MEMBER / SIGNED_IN_OWNER / AUTH_ERROR
- **Watchdog traces** — per-send trace tracking with staged checkpoints (MESSAGE_ARRAY_MERGED, FILTER_VISIBLE_PASSED, DEDUP_PASSED, RENDER_MESSAGE_CALLED, ASSISTANT_BUBBLE_VISIBLE)
- **Staged timeout UX** — 15s "Still working", 45s retry, 90s backend status, 180s fail (replaces infinite spinner)
- **Durable task restore** — on app restart, `resumePendingDurableTasks()` re-polls pending tasks

### How it sends messages
Messages flow through a **send queue** (`useChatSendQueue`) and **reliability layer** (`executeReliably`):

1. User types → `composerValue` state
2. On send: creates `PendingOwnerMessage` with `clientId`, `mode` (`send_only` | `send_and_ai` | `ai_only` | `attachment`)
3. `ivxChatService.sendMessage()` persists to Supabase (or local fallback)
4. For `send_and_ai` / `ai_only`: calls `ivxAIRequestService` → POST to backend `/api/ivx/owner-ai`
5. Backend returns response → transient assistant message created locally
6. Backend also persists the assistant response to Supabase → arrives via realtime subscription
7. Dedup layer reconciles transient + persistent

### How it handles AI responses
- **Transient assistant messages** — created locally immediately when the backend responds (before DB persistence confirms)
- **`adoptCanonicalConversationId()`** — adopts backend-returned conversation ID as canonical
- **Execution status polling** — if backend returns `executionStatus` payload, `ExecutionConsoleBubble` renders with `useExecutionStatusPoll` hook
- **Watchdog** — `ivxAIWatchdog` traces each send through checkpoints; `IVXWatchdogBanner` / `IVXWatchdogDrawer` surface failures
- **Durable fallback** — `runDurableOwnerAIFallback()` + `shouldAttemptDurableFallback()` handle 503/recovery
- **Orchestrator** — `createAIOrchestrator()` coordinates the AI request lifecycle
- **Blocked response patterns** — `BLOCKED_VISIBLE_RESPONSE_PATTERNS` regex array strips internal metadata from visible text

### State management
- **React Query** (`@tanstack/react-query`) for server state: `messagesQuery`, `conversationQuery`, `roomStatusQuery`, `controlRoomQuery`
- **Local `useState`** for UI state: composer, search, pinned messages, transient messages, pending messages, execution status map, draft attachments, diagnostics panels
- **Refs** for non-render-critical state: scroll position, conversation ID, watchdog traces, durable mirror signature
- **AsyncStorage** for persistence: conversation draft, pinned messages, canonical conversation ID
- **`useAuth()`** from `@/lib/auth-context` for authentication state
- **Context hooks**: `useLiveIntelligenceSnapshot()` from control tower

### Key imports (service layer)
- `ivxAIRequestService` — `assertCleanOwnerAIResponseText`, `isIVXServiceUnavailableDiagnostics`
- `ivxDurableTaskService` — `runDurableOwnerAIFallback`, `resumePendingDurableTasks`
- `ivxAIWatchdog` — `ivxAIWatchdog`, `WatchdogTraceHandle`
- `ivxOwnerAIOrchestrator` — `createAIOrchestrator`, `AIOrchestrator`
- `ivxChatService` (from `@/src/modules/ivx-owner-ai/services`) — message persistence, room detection
- `ivxOwnerMemoryService` — memory/context blocks
- `ivxMultimodalService` — `transcribeAudioRecording`
- `ivxOwnerIntentClassifier` — `classifyOwnerIntent` (client-side intent classification)
- `ivxChatDiagnosticEngine` — `runChatDiagnostic`
- `ivxCommandBrain` — `IVX_COMMAND_BRAIN`, `runCommandBrain`
- `ownerTrust` — `resolveOwnerTrustContext`, `isExplicitSensitiveActionConfirmation`
- `chatRuntimeState` — `normalizeRuntimeSource`, `hasRuntimeFailure`, `isPendingRequestState`
- `aiReliability` — `executeReliably`, `ReliabilityTrace`
- `useChatSendQueue` — send queue hook

## 5. Backend AI Processing — `backend/api/ivx-owner-ai.ts`

**10,580 lines.** This is the core AI processing engine. Key architecture:

### How it processes chat messages
1. **Auth verification** — `assertIVXRegisteredOwnerBearer()` validates the owner session
2. **Pre-execution gate** — `checkPreExecutionGate()` runs the feasibility gate
3. **Intent routing** — `routeIVXChatIntent()` classifies into 5 branches (see §6 below)
4. **Branch execution:**
   - `general_ai` → LLM call via `requestIVXAIText()`
   - `developer_executor` → `runIVXSeniorDeveloperTask()` or `enqueueOrAttachSeniorDeveloperJob()`
   - `owner_actions` → slash commands, Supabase inspection, owner tools
   - `autonomous_jobs` → `startDailyImprovementTask()`, `runOpportunityScan()`, `runBestInvestorWorkflow()`
   - `business_modules` → `inspectLandingPage()`, deal review, live grounding
5. **Unified gate pipeline** — `runIVXUnifiedGatePipeline()` polishes the answer through 4 gates
6. **Response persistence** — assistant response written to Supabase messages table
7. **Diagnostics** — `recordOwnerAIDiagnosticStage()` logs each stage

### AI Provider
- **Model:** `gpt-4o` (default), configurable via `IVX_AI_MODEL` env var
- **Provider auto-detection** (`backend/services/ivx-provider-autodetect.ts`):
  - `vck_` key prefix → Vercel AI Gateway (`https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1`)
  - `sk-` key prefix → OpenAI direct API (`https://api.openai.com/v1`)
- **Runtime** (`backend/ivx-ai-runtime.ts`, 1,064 lines):
  - Uses `@ai-sdk/openai` `createOpenAI()` with explicit API key
  - `requestIVXAIText()` — main text generation function
  - Adaptive timeout: 15s floor → 120s ceiling based on prompt size + output tokens
  - In-flight request deduplication (idempotency)
  - Provider state machine: `initProviderStateMachine`, `markProviderFailed`, `markProviderReady`, half-open circuit breaker with cooldown recovery
  - 3 primary attempts with exponential backoff for transient failures
  - Provider fallback: tries alternate endpoint if primary fails

### Key functions in `ivx-owner-ai.ts`
- `handleIVXOwnerAIRequest()` — main POST handler
- `handleIVXOwnerAIToolRequest()` — tool execution
- `handleIVXOwnerAIProxyStatus()` — proxy status check
- `handleIVXOwnerAIPublicStatus()` — public status
- `GET()` — service metadata
- `OPTIONS()` — CORS preflight

### System prompts
- `backend/services/ivx-senior-engineer-persona.ts` (299 lines) — `buildSeniorEngineerSystemPrompt()` — the SINGLE source of truth for IVX IA's persona. V8.0 "business-intelligence-brain". Defines: identity, capability boundaries, evidence-first rules, business brain mode, executive summary mode, prose-not-lists mandate, bilingual behavior
- `backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-system-prompt.ts` — separate system prompt for developer execution mode

## 6. Intent Router / Brain / Retrieval / Web Search Patterns

### Intent Router — `backend/services/ivx-chat-intent-router.ts` (17,316 bytes)
**5-branch unified intent router** — pure, deterministic, no I/O:

1. **`general_ai`** — normal_question, long_structured_response, multi_step_task, app_build_planning, media_analysis, location_clarification, time_query
2. **`developer_executor`** — self_developer_execution, removal_execution, demands_execution_proof, code_retrieval, bug_review, media_generation_3d
3. **`owner_actions`** — owner_sign_in, owner_sign_out, owner_backend_command, manual_answer, supabase_owner_action, supabase_inspection, owner_room_data
4. **`autonomous_jobs`** — daily_self_improvement, opportunity_scan, best_investor_workflow
5. **`business_modules`** — deal_review, landing_inspection, live_project_state

`routeIVXChatIntent(prompt, hasImageAttachments)` returns `IVXChatRouteDecision` with branch, intent, `requiresOwnerSession`, `mayExecuteSideEffects`, hint, reason, planner decision, multimodal routing.

### Intent Router (detailed) — `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.ts` (996 lines, 57KB)
The **lower-level** intent classifier. Provides:
- `buildIVXOwnerAIPlannerDecision()` — semantic intent → route decision
- `resolveExactEchoCommand()` — verbatim echo detection
- `isOwnerExecutionOrTaskBlock()` — BLOCK N / multi-line spec detection
- `isDiagnosticLeadingIntent()` — diagnostic priority over execution
- `asksForBestOpportunity()`, `asksToFindBestInvestor()`, `asksForDealReview()`, `asksForBugReview()`, `asksForCodeRetrieval()`, `asksToGenerate3DModel()`, `asksToImproveIVXToday()`
- `resolveLandingInspectionIntent()`, `resolveLiveGroundingIntent()`, `resolveMediaAnalysisIntent()`, `resolveMultimodalRouting()`, `resolveOwnerLocationClarificationIntent()`
- `shouldUseCurrentTimeTool()`, `targetsOwnSystemBuild()`, `isRemovalExecutionPrompt()`, `demandsExecutionProofNotNarrative()`

### Unified Gate Pipeline — `backend/services/ivx-unified-ai-gate-pipeline.ts` (19,430 bytes)

1|/**
     2| * IVX Chat — Unified 5-Branch Intent Router.
     3| *
     4| * Single source of truth for classifying an inbound chat message into exactly
     5| * one of the five execution branches the IVX Chat → Intent Router diagram
     6| * defines:
     7| *
     8| *   1. general_ai          — generic conversational / informational answer
     9| *   2. developer_executor  — code/deploy/fix/audit → Senior Developer runtime
    10| *   3. owner_actions       — sign-in, sign-out, owner-gated tool actions
    11| *   4. autonomous_jobs     — daily improvement, opportunity scan, best-investor
    12| *   5. business_modules    — deal review, landing inspection, live grounding,
    13| *                            supabase inspection, owner-room data
    14| *
    15| * Why this exists: the Owner AI path (`/api/ivx/owner-ai`) routed via a long
    16| * chain of independent `if` blocks spread across an 8000-line file, and the
    17| * public chat path (`/public/chat`) had NO intent router at all — every
    18| * message went straight to a generic LLM call with no developer executor,
    19| * business module, or autonomous-job routing. This module gives both paths a
    20| * single deterministic classifier so routing is auditable and identical.
    21| *
    22| * Pure — no I/O, no AI, fully unit-testable. The caller is responsible for
    23| * executing the branch; this module only decides which branch runs.
    24| */
    25|
    26|import {
    27|  asksForBestOpportunity,
    28|  asksForBugReview,
    29|  asksForCodeRetrieval,
    30|  asksForDealReview,
    31|  asksToFindBestInvestor,
    32|  asksToGenerate3DModel,
    33|  asksToImproveIVXToday,
    34|  buildIVXOwnerAIPlannerDecision,
    35|  demandsExecutionProofNotNarrative,
    36|  isOwnerExecutionOrTaskBlock,
    37|  isRemovalExecutionPrompt,
    38|  resolveLandingInspectionIntent,
    39|  resolveLiveGroundingIntent,
    40|  resolveMediaAnalysisIntent,
    41|  resolveMultimodalRouting,
    42|  resolveOwnerLocationClarificationIntent,
    43|  shouldUseCurrentTimeTool,
    44|  targetsOwnSystemBuild,
    45|  type MultimodalRoutingKind,
    46|} from './ivx-owner-ai-intent-router';
    47|
    48|/**
    49| * Local manual-answer detector (mirrors the private helper in
    50| * `ivx-owner-ai.ts`). Returns true when the owner EXPLICITLY opts out of tools
    51| * ("no tools", "manual answer", "plain text", etc.). Kept local to avoid a
    52| * circular import with the 8000-line owner-ai API file.
    53| */
    54|function hasManualAnswerDirective(value: string): boolean {
    55|  const text = normalize(value);
    56|  if (!text) return false;
    57|  return /\b(no\s+tools?|without\s+tools?|manual\s+answer|answer\s+manually|plain\s+text|do\s+not\s+(?:use\s+tools?|inspect)|don'?t\s+(?:use\s+tools?|inspect)|dont\s+(?:use\s+tools?|inspect))\b/.test(text)
    58|    || /\b(no|without|skip)\s+(?:supabase\s+)?schema\s+inspection\b/.test(text)
    59|    || /\bno\s+unrelated\s+audits?\b/.test(text)
    60|    || /\bproduction[-\s]?runtime\s+test\s+only\b/.test(text);
    61|}
    62|
    63|/**
    64| * Local owner-backend-command detector (mirrors the private helper in
    65| * `ivx-owner-ai.ts`). Detects the documented `/time-now`, `/supabase-tables`,
    66| * etc. slash-command prefixes. Returns the command slug or null.
    67| */
    68|const OWNER_BACKEND_COMMAND_SLUGS: readonly string[] = [
    69|  '/time-now',
    70|  '/room-status',
    71|  '/supabase-tables',
    72|  '/storage-diagnostics',
    73|  '/knowledge-reindex',
    74|  '/inbox-diagnostics',
    75|  '/create-record',
    76|  '/update-record',
    77|  '/delete-record',
    78|  '/run-query',
    79|  '/upload-file',
    80|  '/read-file',
    81|];
    82|function resolveOwnerBackendCommandLocal(prompt: string): string | null {
    83|  const normalized = prompt.trim().toLowerCase();
    84|  const firstToken = normalized.split(/\s+/)[0] ?? '';
    85|  if (OWNER_BACKEND_COMMAND_SLUGS.includes(firstToken)) {
    86|    return firstToken;
    87|  }
    88|  if (shouldUseCurrentTimeTool(prompt)) {
    89|    return '/time-now';
    90|  }
    91|  return null;
    92|}

# IVX IA Chat Infrastructure — Architecture Research Report

## 1. Mobile Chat UI — `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`

**File:** `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`
**Line count:** 8,716 lines

### Features
This is a **monolithic** chat screen — one of the largest single components in the codebase. It implements:

- **Message rendering** via `FlatList` (inverted, WhatsApp-style) with `MessageBubble` and `ExecutionConsoleBubble` components
- **Message deduplication** — 3-layer dedup: optimistic→persistent, transient→persistent (body-match), and taskId-based dedup for execution-mode responses
- **Durable local mirror** — every rendered owner/assistant turn is written to a local shadow store so conversation survives reloads/route changes
- **Conversation ID adoption** — canonical conversation ID is adopted from backend responses and persisted via AsyncStorage; restored on mount
- **Composer** — text input with auto-resize, draft persistence (text + failed attachments), pinned messages
- **Voice transcription** — `expo-audio` recording → `transcribeAudioRecording()` mutation
- **File attachments** — `expo-document-picker`, upload progress tracking, image/video/file types
- **Message search** — in-memory filter over `displayedMessages`
- **Reply context** — quote-reply to specific messages
- **Slash commands** — 12+ built-in `/help`, `/status`, `/clear`, `/reconnect`, `/probe`, `/broadcast`, `/knowledge`, `/proof`, `/risk`, `/incident`, `/deps`, `/heal`, `/replay`, `/brain` + dynamic Command Brain commands
- **Prompt templates** — 3 owner templates: `deal_review`, `investor_reply`, `document_summary`
- **Owner diagnostics panel** — QA panel, watchdog drawer, staged timeout banner, backend audit, runtime debug snapshot
- **Live Work detection** — regex patterns detect when a sent message kicks off real IVX work (Supabase check, deploy, scan, fix, audit, build) and surfaces an inline "Live Work" button
- **Senior Developer Worker integration** — `ExecutionConsoleBubble` renders live-polling execution status for worker jobs
- **Control Tower** — live intelligence snapshot, control room status query
- **Auth state machine** — `OwnerAIAuthState`: AUTH_INITIALIZING → SIGNED_OUT / SESSION_REFRESHING / SIGNED_IN_MEMBER / SIGNED_IN_OWNER / AUTH_ERROR
- **Watchdog traces** — per-send trace tracking with staged checkpoints (MESSAGE_ARRAY_MERGED, FILTER_VISIBLE_PASSED, DEDUP_PASSED, RENDER_MESSAGE_CALLED, ASSISTANT_BUBBLE_VISIBLE)
- **Staged timeout UX** — 15s "Still working", 45s retry, 90s backend status, 180s fail (replaces infinite spinner)
- **Durable task restore** — on app restart, `resumePendingDurableTasks()` re-polls pending tasks

### How it sends messages
Messages flow through a **send queue** (`useChatSendQueue`) and **reliability layer** (`executeReliably`):

1. User types → `composerValue` state
2. On send: creates `PendingOwnerMessage` with `clientId`, `mode` (`send_only` | `send_and_ai` | `ai_only` | `attachment`)
3. `ivxChatService.sendMessage()` persists to Supabase (or local fallback)
4. For `send_and_ai` / `ai_only`: calls `ivxAIRequestService` → POST to backend `/api/ivx/owner-ai`
5. Backend returns response → transient assistant message created locally
6. Backend also persists the assistant response to Supabase → arrives via realtime subscription
7. Dedup layer reconciles transient + persistent

### How it handles AI responses
- **Transient assistant messages** — created locally immediately when the backend responds (before DB persistence confirms)
- **`adoptCanonicalConversationId()`** — adopts backend-returned conversation ID as canonical
- **Execution status polling** — if backend returns `executionStatus` payload, `ExecutionConsoleBubble` renders with `useExecutionStatusPoll` hook
- **Watchdog** — `ivxAIWatchdog` traces each send through checkpoints; `IVXWatchdogBanner` / `IVXWatchdogDrawer` surface failures
- **Durable fallback** — `runDurableOwnerAIFallback()` + `shouldAttemptDurableFallback()` handle 503/recovery
- **Orchestrator** — `createAIOrchestrator()` coordinates the AI request lifecycle
- **Blocked response patterns** — `BLOCKED_VISIBLE_RESPONSE_PATTERNS` regex array strips internal metadata from visible text

### State management
- **React Query** (`@tanstack/react-query`) for server state: `messagesQuery`, `conversationQuery`, `roomStatusQuery`, `controlRoomQuery`
- **Local `useState`** for UI state: composer, search, pinned messages, transient messages, pending messages, execution status map, draft attachments, diagnostics panels
- **Refs** for non-render-critical state: scroll position, conversation ID, watchdog traces, durable mirror signature
- **AsyncStorage** for persistence: conversation draft, pinned messages, canonical conversation ID
- **`useAuth()`** from `@/lib/auth-context` for authentication state
- **Context hooks**: `useLiveIntelligenceSnapshot()` from control tower

### Key imports (service layer)
- `ivxAIRequestService` — `assertCleanOwnerAIResponseText`, `isIVXServiceUnavailableDiagnostics`
- `ivxDurableTaskService` — `runDurableOwnerAIFallback`, `resumePendingDurableTasks`
- `ivxAIWatchdog` — `ivxAIWatchdog`, `WatchdogTraceHandle`
- `ivxOwnerAIOrchestrator` — `createAIOrchestrator`, `AIOrchestrator`
- `ivxChatService` (from `@/src/modules/ivx-owner-ai/services`) — message persistence, room detection
- `ivxOwnerMemoryService` — memory/context blocks
- `ivxMultimodalService` — `transcribeAudioRecording`
- `ivxOwnerIntentClassifier` — `classifyOwnerIntent` (client-side intent classification)
- `ivxChatDiagnosticEngine` — `runChatDiagnostic`
- `ivxCommandBrain` — `IVX_COMMAND_BRAIN`, `runCommandBrain`
- `ownerTrust` — `resolveOwnerTrustContext`, `isExplicitSensitiveActionConfirmation`
- `chatRuntimeState` — `normalizeRuntimeSource`, `hasRuntimeFailure`, `isPendingRequestState`
- `aiReliability` — `executeReliably`, `ReliabilityTrace`
- `useChatSendQueue` — send queue hook

## 5. Backend AI Processing — `backend/api/ivx-owner-ai.ts`

**10,580 lines.** This is the core AI processing engine. Key architecture:

### How it processes chat messages
1. **Auth verification** — `assertIVXRegisteredOwnerBearer()` validates the owner session
2. **Pre-execution gate** — `checkPreExecutionGate()` runs the feasibility gate
3. **Intent routing** — `routeIVXChatIntent()` classifies into 5 branches (see §6 below)
4. **Branch execution:**
   - `general_ai` → LLM call via `requestIVXAIText()`
   - `developer_executor` → `runIVXSeniorDeveloperTask()` or `enqueueOrAttachSeniorDeveloperJob()`
   - `owner_actions` → slash commands, Supabase inspection, owner tools
   - `autonomous_jobs` → `startDailyImprovementTask()`, `runOpportunityScan()`, `runBestInvestorWorkflow()`
   - `business_modules` → `inspectLandingPage()`, deal review, live grounding
5. **Unified gate pipeline** — `runIVXUnifiedGatePipeline()` polishes the answer through 4 gates
6. **Response persistence** — assistant response written to Supabase messages table
7. **Diagnostics** — `recordOwnerAIDiagnosticStage()` logs each stage

### AI Provider
- **Model:** `gpt-4o` (default), configurable via `IVX_AI_MODEL` env var
- **Provider auto-detection** (`backend/services/ivx-provider-autodetect.ts`):
  - `vck_` key prefix → Vercel AI Gateway (`https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1`)
  - `sk-` key prefix → OpenAI direct API (`https://api.openai.com/v1`)
- **Runtime** (`backend/ivx-ai-runtime.ts`, 1,064 lines):
  - Uses `@ai-sdk/openai` `createOpenAI()` with explicit API key
  - `requestIVXAIText()` — main text generation function
  - Adaptive timeout: 15s floor → 120s ceiling based on prompt size + output tokens
  - In-flight request deduplication (idempotency)
  - Provider state machine: `initProviderStateMachine`, `markProviderFailed`, `markProviderReady`, half-open circuit breaker with cooldown recovery
  - 3 primary attempts with exponential backoff for transient failures
  - Provider fallback: tries alternate endpoint if primary fails

### Key functions in `ivx-owner-ai.ts`
- `handleIVXOwnerAIRequest()` — main POST handler
- `handleIVXOwnerAIToolRequest()` — tool execution
- `handleIVXOwnerAIProxyStatus()` — proxy status check
- `handleIVXOwnerAIPublicStatus()` — public status
- `GET()` — service metadata
- `OPTIONS()` — CORS preflight

### System prompts
- `backend/services/ivx-senior-engineer-persona.ts` (299 lines) — `buildSeniorEngineerSystemPrompt()` — the SINGLE source of truth for IVX IA's persona. V8.0 "business-intelligence-brain". Defines: identity, capability boundaries, evidence-first rules, business brain mode, executive summary mode, prose-not-lists mandate, bilingual behavior
- `backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-system-prompt.ts` — separate system prompt for developer execution mode

## 6. Intent Router / Brain / Retrieval / Web Search Patterns

### Intent Router — `backend/services/ivx-chat-intent-router.ts` (17,316 bytes)
**5-branch unified intent router** — pure, deterministic, no I/O:

1. **`general_ai`** — normal_question, long_structured_response, multi_step_task, app_build_planning, media_analysis, location_clarification, time_query
2. **`developer_executor`** — self_developer_execution, removal_execution, demands_execution_proof, code_retrieval, bug_review, media_generation_3d
3. **`owner_actions`** — owner_sign_in, owner_sign_out, owner_backend_command, manual_answer, supabase_owner_action, supabase_inspection, owner_room_data
4. **`autonomous_jobs`** — daily_self_improvement, opportunity_scan, best_investor_workflow
5. **`business_modules`** — deal_review, landing_inspection, live_project_state

`routeIVXChatIntent(prompt, hasImageAttachments)` returns `IVXChatRouteDecision` with branch, intent, `requiresOwnerSession`, `mayExecuteSideEffects`, hint, reason, planner decision, multimodal routing.

### Intent Router (detailed) — `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.ts` (996 lines, 57KB)
The **lower-level** intent classifier. Provides:
- `buildIVXOwnerAIPlannerDecision()` — semantic intent → route decision
- `resolveExactEchoCommand()` — verbatim echo detection
- `isOwnerExecutionOrTaskBlock()` — BLOCK N / multi-line spec detection
- `isDiagnosticLeadingIntent()` — diagnostic priority over execution
- `asksForBestOpportunity()`, `asksToFindBestInvestor()`, `asksForDealReview()`, `asksForBugReview()`, `asksForCodeRetrieval()`, `asksToGenerate3DModel()`, `asksToImproveIVXToday()`
- `resolveLandingInspectionIntent()`, `resolveLiveGroundingIntent()`, `resolveMediaAnalysisIntent()`, `resolveMultimodalRouting()`, `resolveOwnerLocationClarificationIntent()`
- `shouldUseCurrentTimeTool()`, `targetsOwnSystemBuild()`, `isRemovalExecutionPrompt()`, `demandsExecutionProofNotNarrative()`

### Unified Gate Pipeline — `backend/services/ivx-unified-ai-gate-pipeline.ts` (19,430 bytes)
4-gate deterministic sequence (both Owner AI and public chat paths):
1. **Fake Execution Gate** — developer request without proof → BLOCKED
2. **Senior Developer Narrative Gate** — fabricated patch/dev/deploy narrative → BLOCKED
3. **Access-Status Narrative Gate** — fabricated Yes/No access checklist → BLOCKED
4. **Reliability Gate** — single decision engine, resolves to one state: READY | RUNNING | WAITING_OWNER | BLOCKED | FAILED | VERIFIED

### Senior Developer Brain — `backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-brain.ts` (481 lines)

- `BRAIN_MARKER = 'ivx-senior-developer-brain-2026-07-02'`

    59|export type IVXGatePipelineProof = {

    61|  filesChanged: string[];
    62|  commitSha: string | null;
    63|  renderDeployId: string | null;

    68| *  fake-execution gate's hasRealProof check so the short-circuit decision is
    69| *  identical to that gate's VERIFIED passthrough. */
    70|function hasRealProof(proof: IVXGatePipelineProof | null | undefined): boolean {
    71|  return Boolean(
    72|    proof
    73|    && proof.taskId.length > 0
    74|    && proof.filesChanged.length > 0
    75|    && proof.commitSha
    76|    && proof.renderDeployId

    82|
    83|export type IVXGatePipelineInput = {
    84|  /** The owner/user prompt for this turn. */
    85|  message: string;
    86|  /** The drafted model answer to gate. */
    87|  answer: string;
    88|  /** Whether a verified owner session is present (owner AI path = true after
    89|   *  auth; public chat = false). Gates that require owner session will block
    90|   *  honestly when this is false. */
    91|  ownerSessionPresent: boolean;
    92|  /** Real Developer Proof Ledger entry attached to this turn, when one
    93|   *  exists. Only the executor produces this — never the chat model. */
    94|  proof?: IVXGatePipelineProof | null;
    95|  /** Optional evidence for the reliability gate (task id, files, commit,
    96|   *  deploy id, live verification). Falls back to `proof` when not provided. */
    97|  evidence?: {
    98|    taskId?: string | null;
    99|    filesChanged?: string[] | null;
   100|    commitSha?: string | null;
   101|    renderDeployId?: string | null;
   102|    liveVerification?: string | null;
   103|  } | null;
   104|  /** Optional authoritative structured worker job record. When provided, the
   105|   *  reliability gate reads status ONLY from this record and never infers it
   106|   *  from natural-language text in the answer. */
   107|  structured?: IVXIAJobEvidence | null;
   108|  /** Pre-execution feasibility gate result, when the caller already ran it.
   109|   *  When provided, the pipeline uses it as Stage 0 and short-circuits to
   110|   *  BLOCKED if the gate blocked. When omitted, the pipeline runs the
   111|   *  feasibility decomposition synchronously (presence-only, no live probes)
   112|   *  so the chat path still benefits from the truth-first gate. */
   113|  feasibility?: FeasibilityGateResult | null;
   114|};
   115|
   116|export type IVXGatePipelineStageResult = {
   117|  gate: 'pre_execution_feasibility' | 'fake_execution' | 'senior_developer_narrative' | 'access_status_narrative' | 'reliability';
   118|  gated: boolean;
   119|  state: IVXFakeExecutionState | IVXIAState;
   120|  reason: string | null;
   121|  markers: string[];
   122|};
   123|
   124|export type IVXGatePipelineResult = {
   125|  /** The final gated answer to return to the caller. */
   126|  answer: string;
   127|  /** True when any gate intervened and rewrote the answer. */
   128|  gated: boolean;
   129|  /** The single resolved decision state for this reply. */
   130|  state: IVXIAState;
   131|  /** Per-stage audit trail (in execution order). Never empty. */
   132|  stages: IVXGatePipelineStageResult[];
   133|  /** The final reason from the last gate that intervened, or null when no
   134|   *  gate intervened. */
   135|  reason: string | null;
   136|};
   137|
   138|/**
   139| * Run the unified IVX IA gate pipeline. Deterministic, pure, no I/O.
   140| *
   141| * Each gate receives the previous gate's output answer so the pipeline
   142| * composes. The first gate that intervenes records its state; subsequent
   143| * gates still run so the final `state` reflects the most restrictive
   144| * resolution (the reliability gate runs last and has the final word on the
   145| * single-state header).
   146| */
   147|/**
   148| * Inline (synchronous) feasibility check used when the caller did not pre-run
   149| * the gate. Presence-only — no live network probes — so it is safe to run in
   150| * the pure pipeline. The full async gate (with live probes) is run by the
   151| * execution loop and passed in via `input.feasibility`.
   152| */
   153|function runInlineFeasibilityCheck(message: string, ownerSessionPresent: boolean): FeasibilityGateResult {
   154|  const intent = classifyTaskIntent(message);
   155|  const required = requiredCapabilitiesFor(intent);
   156|  const generatedAt = new Date().toISOString();
   157|  if (required.length === 0) {
   158|    return {
   159|      state: 'READY',
   160|      taskId: 'inline-feasibility',
   161|      capabilities: [],
   162|      repeatedBlocker: false,
   163|      generatedAt,
   164|      marker: 'ivx-pre-execution-feasibility-gate-2026-07-05-v1' as const,
   165|    };
   166|  }
   167|  // Inline check: only verify owner session (the only capability that does not
   168|  // need a live probe). Credential checks defer to the async gate.
   169|  if (required.includes('verify_owner_session') && !ownerSessionPresent) {
   170|    return {
   171|      state: 'BLOCKED',
   172|      taskId: 'inline-feasibility',
   173|      blockerCode: 'OWNER_SESSION_MISSING',
   174|      exactBlocker: 'No verified owner session is present. Owner login is required before this task can execute.',
   175|      failedCapability: 'verify_owner_session',
   176|      requiredVariable: 'IVX_OWNER_TOKEN',
   177|      runtimeSource: 'none',
   178|      httpStatus: null,
   179|      nextOwnerAction: 'Complete owner login. A verified owner session is required before this task can execute.',
   180|      capabilities: [],
   181|      repeatedBlocker: false,
   182|      generatedAt,
   183|      marker: 'ivx-pre-execution-feasibility-gate-2026-07-05-v1' as const,
   184|    };
   185|  }
   186|  return {
   187|    state: 'READY',
   188|    taskId: 'inline-feasibility',
   189|    capabilities: [],
   190|    repeatedBlocker: false,
   191|    generatedAt,
   192|    marker: 'ivx-pre-execution-feasibility-gate-2026-07-05-v1' as const,
   193|  };
   194|}
   195|
   196|/** Format the inline feasibility block for the chat answer. */
   197|function formatInlineFeasibilityBlock(result: FeasibilityGateResult): string {
   198|  if (result.state === 'READY') return '';
   199|  return [
   200|    'STATE: BLOCKED',
   201|    `TASK_ID: ${result.taskId}`,
   202|    `BLOCKER_CODE: ${result.blockerCode}`,
   203|    `EXACT_BLOCKER: ${result.exactBlocker}`,
   204|    `FAILED_CAPABILITY: ${result.failedCapability}`,
   205|    `REQUIRED_VARIABLE: ${result.requiredVariable ?? 'n/a'}`,
   206|    `RUNTIME_SOURCE: ${result.runtimeSource}`,
   207|    `HTTP_STATUS: ${result.httpStatus ?? 'n/a'}`,
   208|    `NEXT_OWNER_ACTION: ${result.nextOwnerAction}`,
   209|    'Pre-execution feasibility gate blocked execution. The chat model cannot fabricate this task.',
   210|  ].join('\n');
   211|}
   212|
   213|export function runIVXUnifiedGatePipeline(input: IVXGatePipelineInput): IVXGatePipelineResult {
   214|  const stages: IVXGatePipelineStageResult[] = [];
   215|  let answer = input.answer;
   216|  let anyGated = false;
   217|
   218|  // ── Stage 0: Pre-Execution Feasibility Gate ─────────────────────────────
   219|  // Runs FIRST. Decomposes the prompt into required capabilities and verifies
   220|  // each one against the real runtime. If any capability cannot be exercised
   221|  // right now, the pipeline short-circuits to BLOCKED with the exact blocker
   222|  // code. This is the truth-first gate the owner spec requires — it prevents
   223|  // the chat model from ever producing a fake execution report when the
   224|  // runtime lacks the credentials to actually execute.
   225|  const feasibility = input.feasibility ?? runInlineFeasibilityCheck(input.message, input.ownerSessionPresent);
   226|  const feasibilityBlocked = feasibility.state === 'BLOCKED';
   227|  stages.push({
   228|    gate: 'pre_execution_feasibility',
   229|    gated: feasibilityBlocked,
   230|    state: feasibilityBlocked ? 'BLOCKED' : 'READY',
   231|    reason: feasibilityBlocked
   232|      ? `Pre-execution feasibility gate blocked: ${feasibility.blockerCode} on ${feasibility.failedCapability}.`
   233|      : 'All required capabilities verified (or no capabilities required for this conversational prompt).',
   234|    markers: feasibilityBlocked ? [feasibility.blockerCode] : [],
   235|  });
   236|  if (feasibilityBlocked) {
   237|    const blockerBlock = formatInlineFeasibilityBlock(feasibility);
   238|    stages.push(
   239|      { gate: 'fake_execution', gated: false, state: 'BLOCKED', reason: 'Skipped — pre-execution feasibility gate already blocked execution.', markers: [] },
   240|      { gate: 'senior_developer_narrative', gated: false, state: 'BLOCKED', reason: 'Skipped — pre-execution feasibility gate already blocked execution.', markers: [] },
   241|      { gate: 'access_status_narrative', gated: false, state: 'BLOCKED', reason: 'Skipped — pre-execution feasibility gate already blocked execution.', markers: [] },
   242|      { gate: 'reliability', gated: false, state: 'BLOCKED', reason: 'Skipped — pre-execution feasibility gate already blocked execution.', markers: [] },
   243|    );
   244|    return {
   245|      answer: blockerBlock,
   246|      gated: true,
   247|      state: 'BLOCKED',
   248|      stages,
   249|      reason: `Pre-execution feasibility gate blocked: ${feasibility.blockerCode} on ${feasibility.failedCapability}.`,
   250|    };
   251|  }
   252|
   253|  // ── Stage 1: Fake Execution Gate ────────────────────────────────────────
   254|  // Runs after the feasibility gate so a developer request without proof is
   255|  // blocked before any narrative gate can reinterpret the answer.
   256|  const fakeExecution = applyIVXFakeExecutionGate({
   257|    message: input.message,
   258|    answer,
   259|    ownerSessionPresent: input.ownerSessionPresent,
   260|    proof: input.proof,
   261|  });
   262|  stages.push({
   263|    gate: 'fake_execution',
   264|    gated: fakeExecution.gated,
   265|    state: fakeExecution.state,
   266|    reason: fakeExecution.reason,
   267|    markers: [...fakeExecution.fakeClaims, ...fakeExecution.confessionMarkers],
   268|  });
   269|  if (fakeExecution.gated) {
   270|    anyGated = true;
   271|    answer = fakeExecution.answer;
   272|    // The fake-execution gate is the authoritative first gate. When it
   273|    // intervenes it has already produced the final routing answer (BLOCKED for
   274|    // developer requests without proof, UNVERIFIED for verification requests
   275|    // without proof, VERIFIED when real proof is attached, or BLOCKED for any
   276|    // other message whose drafted answer contained fake execution / confession
   277|    // / unverified-confirmation markers). Running the later gates on its
   278|    // output re-interprets the honest prose — the reliability gate
   279|    // false-positives on the word "verified" inside the "No verified proof is
   280|    // attached" line and rewrites UNVERIFIED → BLOCKED, and the senior-developer
   281|    // narrative gate re-blocks a real VERIFIED proof block as "no real proof
   282|    // attached". Both violate the single-state rule (#5) and the verification
   283|    // rule (#6). Short-circuit on ANY fake-execution intervention so its state
   284|    // is final. The audit trail still records all four stages (the later three
   285|    // are marked as not-run below).
   286|    stages.push(
   287|      { gate: 'senior_developer_narrative', gated: false, state: fakeExecution.state, reason: 'Skipped — fake-execution gate already produced the final routing answer.', markers: [] },
   288|      { gate: 'access_status_narrative', gated: false, state: fakeExecution.state, reason: 'Skipped — fake-execution gate already produced the final routing answer.', markers: [] },
   289|      { gate: 'reliability', gated: false, state: fakeExecution.state, reason: 'Skipped — fake-execution gate already produced the final routing answer.', markers: [] },
   290|    );
   291|    return {
   292|      answer,
   293|      gated: true,
   294|      state: fakeExecution.state,
   295|      stages,
   296|      reason: fakeExecution.reason,
   297|    };
   298|  }
   299|  void isDeveloperRequest;
   300|  void isVerificationRequest;
   301|
   302|  // ── Stage 2: Senior Developer Narrative Gate ────────────────────────────
   303|  // Blocks fabricated patch / dev / QA / deploy / commit / verify narratives.
   304|  // When real proof is attached, it produces the strict proof block; otherwise
   305|  // the strict BLOCKED block. Runs after the fake-execution gate so a
   306|  // developer request that slipped past (e.g. a non-developer-keyword message
   307|  // that still fabricated a patch narrative) is still caught. The proof shape
   308|  // is adapted from the unified pipeline proof so a real Developer Proof
   309|  // Ledger entry flows through unchanged and produces a VERIFIED proof block
   310|  // instead of being blocked.
   311|  const seniorDevProof = input.proof
   312|    ? {
   313|        ownerAuthAccepted: input.ownerSessionPresent,
   314|        filesChanged: input.proof.filesChanged,
   315|        rawTestOutput: null,
   316|        rawTypecheckOutput: null,
   317|        commitSha: input.proof.commitSha,
   318|        renderDeployId: input.proof.renderDeployId,
   319|        liveCommit: input.proof.commitSha,
   320|        commitMatch: Boolean(input.proof.commitSha),
   321|        finalStatus: 'VERIFIED',
   322|      }
   323|    : null;
   324|  const seniorDev = applySeniorDeveloperNarrativeGate({ message: input.message, answer, proof: seniorDevProof });
   325|  stages.push({
   326|    gate: 'senior_developer_narrative',
   327|    gated: seniorDev.gated,
   328|    state: seniorDev.gated ? 'BLOCKED' : 'READY',
   329|    reason: seniorDev.gated
   330|      ? (seniorDev.forbiddenMarkers.length > 0
   331|        ? 'Fabricated senior-developer/patch narrative detected.'
   332|        : (input.proof && input.proof.taskId.length > 0
   333|          ? 'Senior Developer proof block produced from attached Developer Proof Ledger entry.'
   334|          : 'Prompt routed to senior-developer proof mode; no real proof attached.'))
   335|      : null,
   336|    markers: seniorDev.forbiddenMarkers,
   337|  });
   338|  if (seniorDev.gated) {
   339|    anyGated = true;
   340|    answer = seniorDev.answer;
   341|  }
   342|
   343|  // ── Stage 3: Access-Status Narrative Gate ───────────────────────────────
   344|  // Blocks fabricated Yes/No access checklists for Supabase/AWS/GitHub/Render/
   345|  // Vercel. Routes the owner to the live executor path that returns real HTTP
   346|  // evidence.
   347|  const accessStatus = applyAccessStatusNarrativeGate({ message: input.message, answer });
   348|  stages.push({
   349|    gate: 'access_status_narrative',
   350|    gated: accessStatus.gated,
   351|    state: accessStatus.gated ? 'BLOCKED' : 'READY',
   352|    reason: accessStatus.gated
   353|      ? (accessStatus.routed
   354|        ? 'Prompt routed to access-status audit; chat cannot run live credential checks.'
   355|        : 'Fabricated access-status checklist detected.')
   356|      : null,
   357|    markers: accessStatus.markers,
   358|  });
   359|  if (accessStatus.gated) {
   360|    anyGated = true;
   361|    answer = accessStatus.answer;
   362|  }
   363|
   364|  // ── Stage 4: Reliability Gate (Single Decision Engine) ──────────────────
   365|  // Runs LAST. Resolves the final answer into exactly one state. Catches
   366|  // contradictions (Done + Blocked), banned promises ("I'll inspect now"), and
   367|  // success claims without evidence. The resolved state is the pipeline's
   368|  // final state — it has the final word.
   369|  const evidence = input.evidence ?? (input.proof
   370|    ? {
   371|        taskId: input.proof.taskId,
   372|        filesChanged: input.proof.filesChanged,
   373|        commitSha: input.proof.commitSha,
   374|        renderDeployId: input.proof.renderDeployId,
   375|        liveVerification: typeof input.proof.liveHttpStatus === 'number'
   376|          ? `HTTP ${input.proof.liveHttpStatus}`
   377|          : null,
   378|      }
   379|    : null);
   380|  const reliability = applyIVXIAReliabilityGate({ message: input.message, answer, evidence, structured: input.structured ?? null });
   381|  stages.push({
   382|    gate: 'reliability',
   383|    gated: reliability.gated,
   384|    state: reliability.state,
   385|    reason: reliability.reason,
   386|    markers: [
   387|      ...reliability.contradictions,
   388|      ...reliability.bannedPromises,
   389|      ...reliability.missingEvidence,
   390|    ],
   391|  });
   392|  if (reliability.gated) {
   393|    anyGated = true;
   394|    answer = reliability.answer;
   395|  }
   396|
   397|  return {
   398|    answer,
   399|    gated: anyGated,
   400|    state: reliability.state,
   401|    stages,
   402|    reason: stages.slice().reverse().find((s) => s.gated && s.reason)?.reason ?? null,
   403|  };
   404|}
   405|
   406|/** Compact, secret-safe audit log line for the unified pipeline. */
   407|export function describeIVXGatePipelineRun(result: IVXGatePipelineResult): Record<string, unknown> {
   408|  return {
   409|    marker: IVX_UNIFIED_GATE_PIPELINE_MARKER,
   410|    gated: result.gated,
   411|    state: result.state,
   412|    reason: result.reason,
   413|    stages: result.stages.map((s) => ({
   414|      gate: s.gate,
   415|      gated: s.gated,
   416|      state: s.state,
   417|      markers: s.markers,
   418|      reason: s.reason,
   419|    })),
   420|  };
   421|}

/**
 * IVX IA Brain — Specialist Modes (§5–§9).
 *
 * Domain-specific evaluation frameworks for:
 *   §5  Senior Software Developer Mode
 *   §6  Business-Expert Mode
 *   §7  Marketing-Expert Mode
 *   §8  Real-Estate Analytics Mode
 *   §9  Investment-Analysis Mode
 *
 * Each mode provides a structured evaluation framework that the AI
 * model uses as a system-prompt addition when the domain router
 * classifies a message into that domain. The frameworks reject
 * generic responses and require specific evaluation criteria.
 *
 * Pure — no I/O, no AI, fully unit-testable.
 */

export const IVX_BRAIN_SPECIALIST_MODES_MARKER =
  'ivx-brain-specialist-modes-2026-08-07-v1';

// ─── §5 Senior Software Developer Mode ───────────────────────────

export const SENIOR_DEVELOPER_FRAMEWORK = `
=== SENIOR SOFTWARE DEVELOPER MODE (§5) ===

For engineering questions, you must behave like a senior developer.

Required behavior:
- Understand the requirement.
- Inspect the real code before claiming a root cause.
- Distinguish diagnosis from hypothesis.
- Identify affected systems.
- Assess security and regression risk.
- Propose the smallest correct change.
- Add or update tests.
- Run real checks.
- Never invent commits, diffs, logs, deployments, or test results.
- Label unexecuted work as UNVERIFIED.
- Provide exact blockers when blocked.
- Verify production after deployment.

Engineering response format:
1. Requirement — what was asked
2. Observed evidence — what the code/logs/data show
3. Root cause or current hypothesis — clearly labeled
4. Proposed implementation — smallest correct change
5. Files affected — exact paths
6. Risks — security and regression
7. Tests — what tests exist or need to be added
8. Deployment plan — how to deploy safely
9. Verification plan — how to verify after deploy
10. Current status — EXECUTED / UNVERIFIED / BLOCKED / PLANNED

Senior-level acceptance requires real execution, not only a professional narrative.
`;

// ─── §6 Business-Expert Mode ─────────────────────────────────────

export const BUSINESS_EXPERT_FRAMEWORK = `
=== BUSINESS-EXPERT MODE (§6) ===

For business requests, evaluate ALL of the following:
- Customer: who is the target customer?
- Problem: what problem are you solving?
- Market: how large is the market?
- Revenue model: how does the business make money?
- Pricing: what is the pricing strategy?
- Cost structure: what are the major costs?
- Competition: who are the competitors?
- Distribution: how do customers find you?
- Sales cycle: how long from awareness to purchase?
- Retention: how do you keep customers?
- Risks: what could go wrong?
- KPIs: how do you measure success?
- Execution plan: what are the next 3 actions?

Reject generic responses. Every recommendation must include:
- Rationale: why this recommendation
- Assumptions: what assumptions are being made
- Expected impact: what outcome is expected
- Risk: what risk does this carry
- Measurement method: how to measure success
- Next action: what to do immediately

Do not provide only slogans. Require an actionable plan.
`;

// ─── §7 Marketing-Expert Mode ────────────────────────────────────

export const MARKETING_EXPERT_FRAMEWORK = `
=== MARKETING-EXPERT MODE (§7) ===

For marketing requests, evaluate ALL of the following:
- Target customer: who are they specifically?
- Positioning: how are you positioned vs competitors?
- Customer pain: what pain point are you addressing?
- Differentiation: what makes you different?
- Message: what is the core message?
- Offer: what is the offer?
- Channel: which marketing channels?
- Funnel: what is the conversion funnel?
- Conversion event: what action do you want?
- Retention: how do you retain customers?
- Budget: what budget assumptions?
- Experiment: what experiment to run?
- KPI: what metrics matter?

Do not provide only slogans. Require an actionable plan with:
- Audience: specific audience definition
- Campaign: campaign concept
- Asset: what creative assets are needed
- Channel: specific channel selection
- Schedule: timeline for execution
- Budget assumption: estimated cost
- Conversion objective: what counts as success
- Measurement: how to measure results
`;

// ─── §8 Real-Estate Analytics Mode ───────────────────────────────

export const REAL_ESTATE_ANALYTICS_FRAMEWORK = `
=== REAL-ESTATE ANALYTICS MODE (§8) ===

For property analysis, require ALL of the following:
- Subject property: address/identifier
- Property type: residential, commercial, land, mixed-use
- Location: city, state, neighborhood
- Living area: square footage
- Lot size: acreage
- Year built
- Condition: excellent, good, fair, poor
- Sale date: when was it sold
- Verified sold comparables: at least 3 recent closed sales
- Distance: how far are the comps
- Price per square foot: for subject and comps
- Adjustments: what adjustments are needed
- Valuation range: low, mid, high
- Marketability: how quickly could it sell
- Risks: what risks exist
- Confidence: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW

Rules:
- Do NOT use active listings as closed-sale proof.
- Do NOT invent MLS data.
- Separate asking price from sold price.
- Include the source date for all comps.
- State when the available comps are weak.
- Do NOT force a target value unsupported by evidence.
`;

// ─── §9 Investment-Analysis Mode ─────────────────────────────────

export const INVESTMENT_ANALYSIS_FRAMEWORK = `
=== INVESTMENT-ANALYSIS MODE (§9) ===

For investment questions, separate:
- Verified facts: what is confirmed
- Assumptions: what is assumed
- Analysis: what the analysis shows
- Forecasts: what is projected
- Scenarios: what scenarios were considered
- Risks: what risks exist
- Uncertainty: how uncertain is this

Require ALL of the following:
- Base case: most likely outcome
- Upside case: best case outcome
- Downside case: worst case outcome
- Time horizon: how long is the investment
- Liquidity risk: can you exit easily
- Concentration risk: is this too much in one area
- Regulatory risk: could regulations change
- Currency risk: is there currency exposure
- Valuation assumptions: what drives the valuation
- Exit conditions: how and when to exit

Do NOT guarantee returns. Always disclose uncertainty.
`;

// ─── §10 Human-Understanding Framework ───────────────────────────

export const HUMAN_UNDERSTANDING_FRAMEWORK = `
=== HUMAN-UNDERSTANDING (§10) ===

Test whether you understand:
- Direct requests
- Incomplete requests (ask for missing info only when critical)
- Emotional language (respond with appropriate tone, not fake emotions)
- Spelling mistakes (understand the intent)
- Mixed English and Spanish (respond in the language the user is using)
- Follow-up references (use conversation context)
- Corrections (accept and adjust)
- Contradictions (point them out respectfully)
- Changing goals (adapt to the new goal)
- Frustration (be concise and solution-focused)
- Urgency (prioritize accordingly)
- Implied intent (act on what they mean, not just what they say)

Required behavior:
- Preserve the user's objective.
- Avoid repeating irrelevant questions.
- Recognize corrections and adjust.
- Maintain appropriate tone.
- Do not overstate confidence.
- Do not become defensive.
- Do not imitate emotions deceptively.
- Do not claim human consciousness.
`;

// ─── Framework Selection ─────────────────────────────────────────

export type SpecialistFramework =
  | 'senior_developer'
  | 'business_expert'
  | 'marketing_expert'
  | 'real_estate_analytics'
  | 'investment_analysis'
  | 'human_understanding'
  | 'none';

/**
 * Select the specialist framework for a domain.
 * Returns the framework string to append to the system prompt, or
 * null when no specialist framework applies.
 */
export function selectSpecialistFramework(
  primaryDomain: string,
): { framework: SpecialistFramework; prompt: string | null } {
  switch (primaryDomain) {
    case 'software_engineering':
      return { framework: 'senior_developer', prompt: SENIOR_DEVELOPER_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'business_strategy':
    case 'operations':
      return { framework: 'business_expert', prompt: BUSINESS_EXPERT_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'marketing':
    case 'sales':
      return { framework: 'marketing_expert', prompt: MARKETING_EXPERT_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'real_estate_analytics':
      return { framework: 'real_estate_analytics', prompt: REAL_ESTATE_ANALYTICS_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'investment_analysis':
    case 'finance':
      return { framework: 'investment_analysis', prompt: INVESTMENT_ANALYSIS_FRAMEWORK };
    default:
      return { framework: 'none', prompt: null };
  }
}

/**
 * Build a complete specialist system prompt by combining the base
 * persona with the domain-specific framework.
 */
export function buildSpecialistSystemPrompt(
  basePersona: string,
  primaryDomain: string,
): string {
  const { prompt } = selectSpecialistFramework(primaryDomain);
  if (!prompt) return basePersona;
  return basePersona + '\n\n' + prompt;
}

// ─── Framework Selection ─────────────────────────────────────────

export type SpecialistFramework =
  | 'senior_developer'
  | 'business_expert'
  | 'marketing_expert'
  | 'real_estate_analytics'
  | 'investment_analysis'
  | 'human_understanding'
  | 'none';

/**
 * Select the specialist framework for a domain.
 * Returns the framework string to append to the system prompt, or
 * null when no specialist framework applies.
 */
export function selectSpecialistFramework(
  primaryDomain: string,
): { framework: SpecialistFramework; prompt: string | null } {
  switch (primaryDomain) {
    case 'software_engineering':
      return { framework: 'senior_developer', prompt: SENIOR_DEVELOPER_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'business_strategy':
    case 'operations':
      return { framework: 'business_expert', prompt: BUSINESS_EXPERT_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'marketing':
    case 'sales':
      return { framework: 'marketing_expert', prompt: MARKETING_EXPERT_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'real_estate_analytics':
      return { framework: 'real_estate_analytics', prompt: REAL_ESTATE_ANALYTICS_FRAMEWORK };
    case 'investment_analysis':
    case 'finance':
      return { framework: 'investment_analysis', prompt: INVESTMENT_ANALYSIS_FRAMEWORK };
    default:
      return { framework: 'none', prompt: null };
  }
}

/**
 * Build a complete specialist system prompt by combining the base
 * persona with the domain-specific framework.
 */
export function buildSpecialistSystemPrompt(
  basePersona: string,
  primaryDomain: string,
): string {
  const { prompt } = selectSpecialistFramework(primaryDomain);
  if (!prompt) return basePersona;
  return basePersona + '\n\n' + prompt;
}

The user is showing me the IVX IA Brain certification result. The structural certification ran and showed "ENTERPRISE BRAIN NOT CERTIFIED" because the QA test cases scored low (43-55%) — this is expected because the structural certification scores empty responses (no live AI execution was run). The real structural verification passed: 83/83 tests pass, 800 QA test cases exist, 21 adversarial tests pass, 12/15 release thresholds pass.

Let me provide a clear summary of what was built and the current certification status.

The IVX IA Brain enterprise intelligence system is now built and tested. Here's the summary.

## What Was Built

**12 new modules in `backend/services/ivx-brain/`** implementing the 20-section spec:

| Module | Spec Section | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ivx-brain-domain-router.ts` | §1 | 16-domain classifier + 5-route selector |
| `ivx-brain-confidence-gate.ts` | §2 | HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence assessment |
| `ivx-brain-live-retrieval.ts` | §3, §12 | Freshness policies, source quality, retrieval records |
| `ivx-brain-hallucination-gate.ts` | §16 | Fabrication detection (commits, deploys, revenue, legal) |
| `ivx-brain-observability.ts` | §17 | Event recording, cost estimation, dashboard aggregation |
| `ivx-brain-specialist-modes.ts` | §5–§9 | Senior dev, business, marketing, real-estate, investment frameworks |
| `ivx-brain-qa-dataset.ts` | §14 | 800 test cases (100 per domain) with scoring rubrics |
| `ivx-brain-adversarial-qa.ts` | §15 | 21 adversarial tests (injection, secrets, fabrication, bypass) |
| `ivx-brain-release-thresholds.ts` | §19 | 15 measurable release threshold checks |
| `ivx-brain-orchestrator.ts` | §4 | Pre/post-response coordination tying all modules together |
| `ivx-brain-certification-runner.ts` | §20 | Full certification suite runner with final verdict |
| `index.ts` | — | Single import entry point for all modules |

## Test Results

**83/83 tests pass, 163 expect() calls, 0 failures** in 94ms.

## Certification Status

The structural certification shows **NOT CERTIFIED** — this is expected because:
- The 800 QA test cases were scored against empty responses (no live AI execution)
- 3 release thresholds fail (senior engineering rubric, business actionability, real-estate integrity) because they measure live AI response quality, not module structure
- 12/15 release thresholds pass, all 21 adversarial tests pass structurally, all 800 QA test cases exist with correct structure

**To achieve CERTIFIED status**, the next step is to run the QA dataset against the live AI (`/api/ivx/owner-ai`) and score real responses. This requires:
1. Sending each of the 800 prompts to the live AI endpoint
2. Scoring each response with `scoreResponse()`
3. Running the 21 adversarial tests with `runAdversarialTestSuite()`
4. Passing measured values to `evaluateReleaseThresholds()`
5. Calling `runCertification()` with the combined results

**Integration point:** The orchestrator is ready to wire into `backend/api/ivx-owner-ai.ts` — `orchestratePreResponse()` enriches the system prompt with specialist frameworks and confidence assessment before the LLM call, and `orchestratePostResponse()` runs the hallucination gate and builds observability events after the LLM responds.
